title: Public data and catalog maintenance clients
description: Server-only TypeScript adapters for Frankfurter, NWS, Census, vPIC, Crossref, GLEIF, ROR, Open Food Facts, Open-Meteo, deps.dev, OSV and endoflife.date with injected transport, bounded responses, conditional cache metadata and normalized errors.

notes: Node.js 22+ with standard Fetch, streams, AbortController and a TypeScript build is the supported baseline.
Factories reject browser DOM runtimes; the receiving build must also keep these files in server-only code.
Import and installation do not read credentials, connect providers or install runtime packages.

configuration: Inject a trusted Fetch implementation, application identification and explicit server credential callbacks.
Use a configured HTTPS origin only; never derive origins or credentials from an incoming request.
Census data queries require a key. Open-Meteo hosted access requires an explicit noncommercial or customer subscription profile.
Configure request deadlines and decoded response byte limits; retries are opt-in and bounded.
Applications own caching, cross-process quotas, source attribution, authorization and live acceptance.
limitations: Only documented operations and returned fields are supported; these are original adapters rather than full provider SDKs.
No shared cache storage, key provisioning, billing setup, background scheduling, offline dataset mirrors or source-rights clearance is included.
HTTP metadata does not establish freshness once cached by the receiving application; revalidate according to provider headers and terms.
Only injected mock-transport fixtures are exercised here. Live provider uptime, credentials, quotas, legal suitability and deployment acceptance remain application checks.
decisions: results are {notModified, data, meta}; a 304 gives data: null and caching is the app's job
retries off by default (max 2, only 429/502/503/504); 15 s total timeout; 1 MiB response cap
a provider 404 is a PublicDataError, not an empty record; redirects are refused
